gen-dafont-eraser-gf-lexend-exa: Eraser hits hard with bold, uniform strokes and no fuss. Lexend Exa follows in a plain sans with wide curves and a big x-height, so a slightly larger heading keeps the two from competing.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga spaces its letters generously, with flat single-weight lines and ascenders that barely rise above the lowercase. And Eraser's heavy, uniform heading sits over it like a stamp, so the text below feels loose, wide and easy to drift through.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-lexend-mega: Eraser's letters are heavy and uniform, with no thick-to-thin shifts at all. Lexend Mega is a plain sans with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals, so nudging its size down a touch gives the heading more room to lead.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta brings big, generous lowercase with curves that never thin out and tight room for ascenders. Lexend Peta is a plain sans that takes the heavy, understated Eraser heading and lets it speak first while the text stays approachable beneath.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-lexend-tera: Understated is the first word for Eraser, whose bold letters never swell or thin, set above Lexend Tera's plotter-pen line. Wide-spaced, open and contemporary, the sans-serif text gives the heavy heading breathing room.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-lexend-zetta: Eraser is blunt, heavy and uniform in every stroke. Its job is punch, while Lexend Zetta, a sans-serif of ribbon-like lines, tall small letters and wide tracking, does the quieter work of staying friendly across the text.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-montserrat-alternat: Montserrat Alternates reads open and contemporary, its round letters matching their stems and its lowercase crowding up toward the capital line. And Eraser's heavy, understated heading sits above it with moderate height, giving the sans text a firm anchor to hang from.
gen-dafont-exoplanet-poppins: Exoplanet's tightly shut c, e and s give it a sleek, cosmic look, like toothpaste squeezed in one line. Poppins is the sans that opens things back up, its loose curves and sturdy lowercase doing the day-to-day reading the heading doesn't.
gen-dafont-good-times-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono lines its letters up like pins in a wide board, with curves as thick as its stems. And Good Times, stencil-cut with mildly varied bars, sits over it as the commanding, geometric voice the sans-serif text quietly supports.
gen-dafont-good-times-gf-julius-sans-one: Commanding and geometric, Good Times has a gapped e and heavy small letters, with a mild pen-like variation in weight. But Julius Sans One is the sans-serif that stands out, with big spaces between letters and curves that stay one thickness.
